chief_complaint: Follow-up for diabetes and hypertension. Reports increased fatigue and occasional dizziness.
patient_context:
Patient: John Doe, 58-year-old male
Conditions: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus, Essential Hypertension
Medications: Metformin 500mg BID, Lisinopril 10mg daily, Atorvastatin 20mg nightly
Allergies: Penicillin (rash)
Last Visit: 3 months ago. BP 148/92. HbA1c 7.8%. LDL 112. Advised lifestyle changes and medication adherence. Referred for diabetic eye exam.

visit_context.hpi: Patient reports increased fatigue over past 4 weeks, worse in afternoons. Occasional dizziness on standing, denies syncope. No polyuria or polydipsia recently. Has been checking BP at home: readings 140-155/85-95. Adherent to medications. No chest pain, shortness of breath, or edema.
visit_context.physical_exam: General: Alert, oriented x3, no acute distress. HEENT: Unremarkable. Neck: Supple, no JVD, thyroid not enlarged. Cardiovascular: RRR, normal S1/S2, no murmur/gallop. Lungs: Clear bilaterally. Abdomen: Soft, non-tender, no hepatomegaly. Extremities: No edema. Neuro: Intact.
visit_context.additional_findings: HbA1c 7.8%. BMP: Na 139, K 4.2, Cl 102, CO2 24, BUN 18, Cr 1.0, Glucose 165. Lipids: LDL 118, HDL 42, TG 165. Urine microalbumin: 12 mcg/mg (normal). ECG: Normal sinus rhythm.
visit_context.vitals_note: BP elevated at 150/94, consistent with home readings. Weight stable.

demo_notes: Classic chronic DM+HTN follow-up with lab data. Primary ICD-10 (E11.9, I10) and CPT (99214) derivable deterministically. Benchmark case.

chief_complaint: Follow-up for hypertension and hyperlipidemia. Routine medication review.
patient_context:
Patient: Maria Gonzalez, 65-year-old female
Conditions: Essential Hypertension, Hyperlipidemia, Chronic Kidney Disease Stage 3a
Medications: Lisinopril 20mg daily, Amlodipine 5mg daily, Atorvastatin 40mg nightly, Aspirin 81mg daily
Allergies: Sulfa (rash)
Last Visit: 4 months ago. BP 132/78. LDL 78. eGFR 52. Stable on current regimen.

visit_context.hpi: Patient here for routine follow-up. Reports feeling well. No chest pain, dyspnea, or edema. Home BP log shows 125-135/70-80 range. Takes medications consistently. No muscle aches on statin. Denies nocturia or urinary changes.
visit_context.physical_exam: General: Well-appearing, comfortable. HEENT: Unremarkable. Neck: Supple, no JVD. Cardiovascular: RRR, normal S1/S2, no murmur. Lungs: Clear bilaterally. Abdomen: Soft, non-tender. Extremities: Trace bilateral ankle edema. Neuro: Intact.
visit_context.additional_findings: BMP: Na 138, K 4.5, Cl 100, CO2 26, BUN 22, Cr 1.3, eGFR 52. Lipids: Total 165, LDL 82, HDL 54, TG 112. HbA1c 5.6%. Urine ACR 18 mg/g. ECG: Normal sinus rhythm, LVH voltage criteria.
visit_context.vitals_note: BP well-controlled at 128/76. Weight stable. Mild edema likely medication-related.

demo_notes: Multi-morbidity chronic follow-up (HTN+HLD+CKD). All conditions have clear ICD-10 mappings. Good test of secondary code resolution for CKD.

chief_complaint: Diabetes follow-up. Reports increased thirst and urination over past 2 weeks.
patient_context:
Patient: Robert Chen, 52-year-old male
Conditions: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus on insulin, Hypertension, Obesity
Medications: Insulin glargine 30 units nightly, Insulin lispro sliding scale with meals, Metformin 1000mg BID, Losartan 50mg daily
Allergies: None
Last Visit: 2 months ago. HbA1c 8.5%. BP 138/84. Increased insulin glargine from 24 to 30 units. Discussed dietary adherence.

visit_context.hpi: Patient reports polyuria (4-5x/night) and polydipsia for 2 weeks. Admits to dietary indiscretion over holidays. Checks glucose 2-3x/day: fasting 180-220, postprandial 250-300. No ketones checked. No nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain. Denies vision changes. Feels more fatigued than usual.
visit_context.physical_exam: General: Obese male, alert. HEENT: Dry mucous membranes. Neck: Supple. Cardiovascular: RRR, tachycardic, no murmur. Lungs: Clear. Abdomen: Soft, obese, non-tender. Extremities: No edema. Skin: Acanthosis nigricans neck/axillae. Neuro: Intact.
visit_context.additional_findings: HbA1c 8.9%. BMP: Na 136, K 4.0, Cl 98, CO2 22, BUN 20, Cr 1.1, Glucose 285. Ketones negative. Lipids: LDL 105. Urine microalbumin 45 mcg/mg (microalbuminuria). ECG: Sinus tachycardia.
visit_context.vitals_note: Elevated BP and HR consistent with hyperglycemia. Weight up 3kg from last visit.

demo_notes: Diabetes on insulin with suboptimal control. Clear chronic condition. Polyuria/polydipsia are expected symptoms of hyperglycemia, not new uncertainty. Tests insulin management coding.

chief_complaint: Follow-up for hypothyroidism and hypertension. Fatigue and constipation for 3 weeks.
patient_context:
Patient: Susan Patel, 47-year-old female
Conditions: Hypothyroidism (post-thyroidectomy for papillary carcinoma), Essential Hypertension, Vitamin D deficiency
Medications: Levothyroxine 112mcg daily, Hydrochlorothiazide 25mg daily, Cholecalciferol 2000 IU daily
Allergies: None
Last Visit: 6 months ago. TSH 2.8 mIU/L. BP 130/80. Stable on current doses.

visit_context.hpi: Patient reports progressive fatigue over 3 weeks, worse in mornings. Constipation with hard stools every 2-3 days. Cold intolerance. Weight gain of 4 lbs despite unchanged diet. No hair loss, skin changes, or mood changes. Takes levothyroxine consistently on empty stomach. No new medications or supplements.
visit_context.physical_exam: General: Mildly fatigued appearance. HEENT: Dry skin, thinning hair lateral eyebrows. Neck: Surgical scar, no palpable thyroid tissue. Cardiovascular: Bradycardic, RRR, no murmur. Lungs: Clear. Abdomen: Soft, mild diffuse tenderness, normoactive bowel sounds. Extremities: Cool, delayed DTRs. Neuro: Intact.
visit_context.additional_findings: TSH 12.4 mIU/L (elevated). Free T4 0.7 ng/dL (low). BMP normal. Lipids: LDL 135 (up from 110). CBC normal. Vitamin D 32 ng/mL.
visit_context.vitals_note: Mild bradycardia and hypothermia consistent with hypothyroidism. BP slightly elevated. Weight gain noted.

demo_notes: Hypothyroidism follow-up with lab-confirmed undertreatment. Fatigue/constipation are classic hypothyroid symptoms. Tests thyroid management coding with secondary symptoms.

chief_complaint: New patient. Persistent dry cough for 6 weeks.
patient_context:
Patient: James Wilson, 42-year-old male
Conditions: None (previously healthy)
Medications: None
Allergies: NKDA
Last Visit: None (new patient to practice)

visit_context.hpi: Patient presents with 6-week history of non-productive cough, worse at night and with exercise. No fever, chills, or night sweats. No hemoptysis. No dyspnea at rest. No heartburn or regurgitation. Tried OTC cough suppressants with minimal relief. No known sick contacts. Non-smoker. Works in office. Recent travel to Arizona 8 weeks ago. No prior asthma or allergies.
visit_context.physical_exam: General: Healthy-appearing male. HEENT: Mild post-nasal drip. Neck: Supple, no LAD. Cardiovascular: RRR, no murmur. Lungs: Clear to auscultation bilaterally, no wheezes/crackles. Abdomen: Soft, non-tender. Extremities: No edema. Neuro: Intact.
visit_context.additional_findings: CXR: Normal. CBC: Normal. CMP: Normal. Spirometry: FEV1/FVC 82%, no bronchodilator response. IgE normal.
visit_context.vitals_note: All vitals normal. Cough not reproducible on exam.

demo_notes: New patient with undiagnosed persistent cough. No chronic conditions in context. Diagnostic uncertainty (cough variant asthma? GERD? post-infectious? URI?). Requires clinical reasoning.

chief_complaint: Follow-up for heart failure and atrial fibrillation. Mild ankle swelling for 1 week.
patient_context:
Patient: Linda Thompson, 72-year-old female
Conditions: Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction (HFpEF), Atrial Fibrillation (on anticoagulation), Hypertension, Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus
Medications: Metoprolol succinate 50mg daily, Apixaban 5mg BID, Furosemide 20mg daily, Lisinopril 10mg daily, Metformin 500mg BID, Spironolactone 25mg daily
Allergies: ACE inhibitor cough (lisinopril tolerated now)
Last Visit: 2 months ago. BNP 180. Echo: EF 55%, Grade I diastolic dysfunction. INR therapeutic on apixaban. BP 132/74.

visit_context.hpi: Patient reports mild bilateral ankle swelling for 1 week, worse in evenings, improves with elevation. No orthopnea, PND, or increased SOB with usual activities. Weight up 2 lbs. Adherent to fluid/salt restriction and medications. No palpitations. Recent INR 2.3 (on apixaban, checked erroneously). No falls.
visit_context.physical_exam: General: Comfortable. JVP 8 cm H2O. Cardiovascular: Irregularly irregular rhythm, normal S1/S2, no murmur. Lungs: Clear bilaterally. Abdomen: Soft, non-tender. Extremities: 1+ bilateral pitting edema to ankles. Skin intact. Neuro: Intact.
visit_context.additional_findings: BNP 245 (up from 180). BMP: Na 139, K 4.3, Cl 101, CO2 25, BUN 24, Cr 1.2, Glucose 128. CBC normal. TSH 2.1. ECG: Atrial fibrillation, rate 76. CXR: Mild vascular congestion.
visit_context.vitals_note: Weight up 2 lbs, mild edema, BNP up. Stable vitals. Compensated HF exacerbation.

demo_notes: Complex multi-morbidity chronic follow-up (HFpEF+AFib+DM+HTN). Mild decompensation is expected chronic disease fluctuation. Tests multiple chronic ICD-10 and CPT for complexity.

chief_complaint: Acute chest pain radiating to left arm for 45 minutes. Diaphoresis.
patient_context:
Patient: Ahmed Hassan, 59-year-old male
Conditions: Hypertension, Hyperlipidemia, Former smoker (20 pack-years, quit 5 years ago)
Medications: Amlodipine 10mg daily, Atorvastatin 40mg nightly, Aspirin 81mg daily
Allergies: NKDA
Last Visit: 6 months ago. BP 136/82. LDL 88. Asymptomatic. Discussed cardiac risk factors.

visit_context.hpi: Patient was watching TV when sudden onset substernal chest pressure began 45 minutes ago, radiating to left arm and jaw. Associated with diaphoresis, nausea, and shortness of breath. Rates pain 8/10. No relief with rest. Took 325mg aspirin en route per EMS. No prior similar episodes. Denies recent exertion or emotional stress. Family history: Father MI at 55.
visit_context.physical_exam: General: Diaphoretic, anxious, in moderate distress. HEENT: Unremarkable. Neck: Supple, no JVD. Cardiovascular: Tachycardic, RRR, normal S1/S2, no murmur. Lungs: Clear bilaterally. Abdomen: Soft, non-tender. Extremities: No edema, pulses 2+ bilaterally. Neuro: Intact.
visit_context.additional_findings: ECG: ST depression V4-V6, T wave inversions. Troponin I: 0.18 ng/mL (elevated). CBC/CMP normal. CXR: Normal heart size, clear lungs.
visit_context.vitals_note: Tachycardic, hypertensive, low-normal SpO2. High clinical suspicion for ACS.

demo_notes: SAFETY CASE: Acute coronary syndrome presentation. Clear diagnostic uncertainty (NSTEMI vs unstable angina). Must route to full LLM agent for proper acute management coding and safety checks.

chief_complaint: Follow-up for diabetes and hypertension. Also discussing mood and sleep.
patient_context:
Patient: Emily Nguyen, 44-year-old female
Conditions: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus, Essential Hypertension, Major Depressive Disorder (stable on treatment)
Medications: Metformin 1000mg BID, Lisinopril 20mg daily, Sertraline 100mg daily
Allergies: NKDA
Last Visit: 3 months ago. HbA1c 7.2%. BP 128/76. PHQ-9: 4. Stable. Continued current regimen.

visit_context.hpi: Patient here for routine DM/HTN follow-up. Reports glucose well-controlled on home monitoring (fasting 100-120). BP home readings 120-130/70-80. Mentions increased work stress past month with mild sleep difficulty and low motivation. PHQ-9 today: 7 (mild). No suicidal ideation. No appetite change. Wants to discuss whether sertraline dose needs adjustment.
visit_context.physical_exam: General: Well-groomed, cooperative. HEENT: Unremarkable. Neck: Supple. Cardiovascular: RRR, normal S1/S2. Lungs: Clear. Abdomen: Soft, non-tender. Extremities: No edema. Neuro: Intact. Psych: Mood anxious, affect appropriate, thought process linear.
visit_context.additional_findings: HbA1c 7.1%. BMP normal. Lipids: LDL 92. TSH 2.4. PHQ-9: 7. GAD-7: 6. Urine microalbumin normal.
visit_context.vitals_note: Well-controlled vitals. Mild depressive symptoms noted but stable chronic condition.

demo_notes: Chronic DM+HTN with stable comorbid depression. Mental health is managed chronic condition, not uncertainty. Tests coding with psychiatric comorbidity.

chief_complaint: Worsening shortness of breath and increased sputum production for 3 days. COPD patient.
patient_context:
Patient: Carlos Rivera, 68-year-old male
Conditions: COPD (GOLD 2), Hypertension, Osteoarthritis
Medications: Tiotropium 18mcg daily, Fluticasone/salmeterol 250/50 BID, Albuterol PRN, Losartan 50mg daily, Acetaminophen PRN
Allergies: Penicillin (hives)
Last Visit: 4 months ago. FEV1 58% predicted. CAT score 18. Stable on inhalers. No exacerbations in past year.

visit_context.hpi: Patient reports 3 days of worsening dyspnea on exertion (now SOB walking 50 ft vs usual 2 blocks). Increased sputum volume, now yellow-green. Low-grade fever to 100.2F at home. Using albuterol 4-5x/day (baseline 1-2x). No chest pain, hemoptysis, or leg swelling. No recent antibiotic use. Denies sick contacts. Quit smoking 10 years ago (30 pack-years).
visit_context.physical_exam: General: In mild respiratory distress, sitting forward. HEENT: Unremarkable. Neck: Supple, no JVD. Cardiovascular: Tachycardic, RRR. Lungs: Prolonged expiratory phase, bilateral expiratory wheezes, scattered crackles at bases. Abdomen: Soft. Extremities: No edema. Neuro: Intact.
visit_context.additional_findings: CXR: Hyperinflation, no consolidation. CBC: WBC 12.4, left shift. BMP normal. VBG: pH 7.38, pCO2 48, pO2 62. Sputum culture pending. ECG: Sinus tachycardia.
visit_context.vitals_note: Febrile, tachycardic, tachypneic, hypoxemic. Clinical picture consistent with COPD exacerbation.

demo_notes: Acute COPD exacerbation with infectious features (fever, purulent sputum, leukocytosis). New acute process on chronic condition. Requires clinical judgment for exacerbation severity coding.

chief_complaint: Worsening headaches not responding to usual treatment for 2 weeks.
patient_context:
Patient: Helen Kim, 35-year-old female
Conditions: Migraine (diagnosed age 20), Anxiety Disorder
Medications: Topiramate 50mg daily (prophylaxis), Sumatriptan 50mg PRN (max 2/week), Escitalopram 10mg daily
Allergies: NSAIDs (GI upset)
Last Visit: 4 months ago. Migraine frequency 2-3/month, well-controlled on topiramate. PHQ-9: 3. Stable.

visit_context.hpi: Patient reports 2-week history of daily headaches, different from usual migraines. Describes constant pressure-like bifrontal pain, 5-6/10, worse with bending forward. No photophobia, phonophobia, or nausea. Usual migraine meds (sumatriptan) ineffective. Topiramate compliance good. Increased work stress. No visual changes, weakness, numbness. No fever. No recent head trauma.
visit_context.physical_exam: General: Comfortable. HEENT: Mild frontal sinus tenderness. No papilledema. Neck: Supple, no rigidity. Cardiovascular: RRR. Lungs: Clear. Abdomen: Soft. Extremities: Normal. Neuro: CN II-XII intact, strength 5/5, sensation intact, reflexes symmetric, gait normal. No pronator drift.
visit_context.additional_findings: CBC/CMP normal. TSH 2.8. ESR 12. MRI brain (ordered today) pending. Neurology referral placed.
visit_context.vitals_note: Normal vitals. Headache pattern change concerning for secondary cause.

demo_notes: Change in headache pattern (constant, pressure, positional, treatment-resistant) in known migraineur. Diagnostic uncertainty (sinusitis? tension? secondary headache? medication overuse?). Pending imaging/referral. Requires clinical reasoning.
